result.topic_en: Riemann's notes on the hydrodynamic equations for air waves along particle paths, forming characteristic-type combinations, and then a solution of the Riemann function for $\partial^2 v/\partial p\partial q + v = 0$ by a power series and representation by a definite integral.
result.transcription:
$du = -a^2\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}(dx - u\,dt) + \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}(dy - v\,dt) + \frac{\partial u}{\partial z}(dz - w\,dt) = a^2 \frac{\partial \log\varrho}{\partial x} dt$
$d\log\varrho = \frac{\partial \log\varrho}{\partial x}(dx - u\,dt) + \frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial y}(dy - v\,dt) + \frac{\partial \log\varrho}{\partial z}(dz - w\,dt) - \frac{\partial u}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\,dt$

$\alpha\left(\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial x} + \alpha\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} + \beta\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} + \gamma\frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\right)$
$\beta\left(\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial y} + \alpha\frac{\partial u}{\partial y} \quad\right)$
$\gamma\left(\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial z} + \alpha \cdots \right)$

$\frac{\partial(\log\varrho + \alpha u + \beta v + \gamma w)}{\partial x} x' + \cdots y' \quad z' + \frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial t} + \alpha\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} + \beta\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + \gamma\frac{\partial w}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial t}u + \frac{\partial\beta}{\partial t}v + \frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial t}w$

Man erhält also
$w_{p',q'} = \cdots$ oder, durch partielle Integration, auch
$v_{p'q'} = (vw)_{p',q'} + \int_{q',s}^{p',s} \left\{ v\left(\frac{\partial w}{\partial p} + w\right)dp + w\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial q} + v\right)dq \right\}$
$= (vw)_{p',s} + \int_{q',s}^{p',s} w\left(v - \frac{\partial v}{\partial p}\right)dp + v\left(w - \frac{\partial w}{\partial q}\right)dq$
$=$
Da in der Curve $s$ [?] $w$ und [-dessen Differentialquot.-] dann auch die in dem {+gegebene+} [-Ausdruck-] [?] sind, so erhält man [?] Ausdrücke
auf der rechten Seite außer der Function $v$ nur bekannte
Größen
und [-also-] die Aufgabe ist also gelöst, wenn
[-für-] den Bedingungen genügt [?] wird.
Setzt man $v = f((p - p')(q - q'))$ und
$f(p \cdot q) = e^{p-q}$ [?], so geht die Bedingungen über
in $\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial p\partial q} + v = 0 \quad p = 0\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial q} = 0 \quad q = 0\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial p} = 0 \quad (p = 0, q = 0)\ v = 1$
Ebenso [?] $v = \sum_0^\infty \frac{p^n q^n (-1)^n}{n!\,n!}$ genügt {+den Bedingungen+}
Man erhält also für $v$ den Ausdruck
[-$\triangleright$-] $e^{(p - p')(q-q')} \sum_0^\infty$
